rules: Conventional prefix (feat/fix/chore/refactor/docs/test, no scopes); small atomic commits, one purpose each.
AI-assisted commits carry an Assisted-by trailer (kernel format); never Co-Authored-By for AI.
Commit as the human: an agent or autonomous run sets its git identity to the person responsible, never the tool's name or a bot address.

Outward text (a pull-request body, an issue, a comment) carries no agent-session URL and no tool 'generated with' footer: after creating one, re-read what was posted and strip either shape the harness appended.
Substantive work goes on a branch + PR; never force-push, never --no-verify.
Never commit or push unless asked.
Markdown is the single source of truth; HTML is a generated, disposable artefact.
Docs are present tense only — what IS, never what was superseded or planned.
One Diataxis type per page (tutorial / how-to / reference / explanation).
User-facing prose in British English; code-side identifiers, comments, strings in US English.

Phases and milestones are retired: sequencing is dependencies (blocked_by, builds_on) plus the lifecycle shelves, rendered as the Now / Next / Later status block; the checkpoint is the derived release plus each intent's acceptance criteria; an intent that must land by a cut carries target_release, which the cut reports and moves forward.
No time estimates and no roadmap document: the press-release intent format carries priority, and the word roadmap is retired.
Capture issues to the ledger via `abcd capture`; folder membership is the status signal.
Never fix ahead of an armed detector — record the finding first.
Intents are press-release-first; acceptance criteria are BDD (Given/When/Then).

Personas take their names from an open alphabetical sequence — Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, and on — that the repository extends when it needs another; where the repository declares a persona roster (the `registry` file its `persona_registry` lint rule names in `.abcd/docs-lint.json`), take each persona's name and role from that roster and pick by role.
Lifecycle is drafts/ -> planned/ -> shipped/; a planned intent's adoption is the product thinker's decision.

The change that lands a planned intent's work closes its spec in the same change (abcd spec close <spc-N>), which ships the intent; nothing runs it for you, and a planned intent whose code is on main is invisible to the release cut.

Background load (burners, busy loops, stress runs) starts as ONE owned process group and is killed as a group, so a failed bookkeeping step cannot orphan it: in bash (zsh refuses job control without a terminal) wrap the whole load in one subshell job, `set -m; ( burner & burner & wait ) & pg=$!`, because a loop of separate `&` jobs gives each job its own group and the group kill then reaches only the last. An agent's shell state does not survive between tool calls, so `pg` lives in a file the session owns and is re-checked before use: `kill -- -"$pg"` only once `ps -o pgid= -p "$pg"` still prints `$pg` and `ps -o comm= -p "$pg"` names the shell that launched the load, so a stale or reused pid is never signalled. Never kill by pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`): a pattern also matches other sessions' processes, and one took down peer sessions' gates on 2026-09-23. Never `nohup` with a list of pids in a file as the only handle: orphaned burners have starved a development machine into a kernel panic.

Clean is proven by checking what is actually running, never by having read the list of what was started: `pgrep -g "$pg"` and `pgrep -x <burner name>` both return nothing before the machine is called clean.

A load experiment on a live development machine needs the user's explicit consent first and a hard cap below the core count (`getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN`), leaving cores free for the operating system's own daemons.

Gate a preflight or a race run on a shared machine with abcd's waiter, never a hand-written waiter loop. `make preflight` gates itself, so it needs no wrapper: it waits once, as one whole run, before any of its stages, at `abcd implement load --wait`, which stays shut while the one-minute load is at your account's wait limit, another `go test -race` run is live, another `make preflight` is running, or another waiter is queued ahead of it (one that started earlier, whatever its pid, or within two seconds of it with the lower pid) or running its command, under any account. It reads all of that from the process table, which shows every account's processes: no file another account can write is read; the gate reads only the process table. A waiter queued ahead of yours still delays yours, under any account, until it opens or reaches its own timeout (it may be shut by its own account's stricter wait limit), and a waiter running its command holds every later gate for the command's length, by design; the one exception is a waiter ahead with a higher pid, as after the process ids wrap, which may run an abcd from v0.15.0 or earlier that waits on every lower pid and so on yours, so once such waiters alone have kept yours shut for five minutes on end (and a step more for each such waiter ahead beyond the first, so the earlier of two behind one opens first), yours stops counting them. Once clear it waits a random 15 to 60 seconds and checks everything again before it opens, so two starters in one quiet minute do not start together, and each test stage then takes a `go test -p` derived from the online cores and the load. Before its race stage it waits again at `abcd implement load --race-gate` (never spelt with `--wait`, which an older abcd reads as a first gate's waiter): at one preflight at a time it opens at once, and above that it stays shut while another `go test -race` run or a race waiter queued ahead of it (by the same rule) is live, the load is at the limit, or the race gate's own hold is in force (another race waiter of your account opened within two minutes; a first gate's hold never shuts the race gate, nor a race gate's hold the first gate), so race stages are kept apart among the preflights whose checkouts have that gate, one race stage at a time within your account and across accounts all but a narrow window (a race waiter gone before its race run shows, or, after a pid wrap, two waiters whose start and pid disagree: one running v0.15.1, which counts a waiter ahead only with the lower pid as well, or two of the start order whose whole-second ages read a tie differently or the later of which stopped counting the earlier past its five-minute cap); an account at one opens its race gate at once whatever another account set; a checkout older than the gate runs its race stage ungated, so set more than one only once no such checkout runs a preflight. How many preflights the first gate admits at once is your own machine's setting, `load.preflights` in `~/.abcd.noindex/config.json` (or `ABCD_LOAD_PREFLIGHTS` in the environment, for a trial), one by default, four at most, and never read from a repository file, so a checkout cannot raise the machine's load; a `config.json` that cannot be read for it is read past, one preflight at a time applies, and the gate names the file, the cause and the fix on stderr, so only a `load.preflights` that is there and unusable refuses the wait; above one, the first gate admits a preflight while fewer than that many others are running (a preflight queued at its race gate runs nothing and takes no slot until its race run starts), a live race run does not shut it by itself, and each stage's `-p` is at most the cores divided by it. Gate a lone race run with the command form, `abcd implement load --wait -- go test -race ./...`: to every other waiter it is running its command for the command's length (with one preflight at a time that shuts every first gate, and above one it takes a slot), and because its command is a race run it waits as a race stage does, shut while another race run is live whatever the setting, and counts as a race run to every race gate and every other such run from the moment it opens. Run a package's tests the same way, `abcd implement load --wait -- go test ./internal/<pkg>/`: a plain `go test` never waits at the gate, so it holds the load up for every gated run, and the waiting line names it by pid. On 2026-10-11 a loop built on `pgrep -f "go test -race"` matched its own shell, whose command line carries that string, so it saw a race run forever and never opened; and loops sharing one release condition opened together and put four race runs on 16 cores at once. The waiter judges each process by its arguments with its own ancestry excluded, and admits one waiter at a time, with one exception it narrows: across accounts, which share no hold, two waiters can open in one moment, so the command form looks once more two seconds after it opens and stands back from the other unless it started earlier and has the lower pid too (the later start stands back whatever the pids, and the earlier one from a lower pid as well, which an older abcd runs past), re-draws its jitter and waits again (at most three times) while the other runs.
The lifeboat is the floor of recoverable theory, not the theory itself (Naur) — hunt the originating session.
Runtime artefacts stay in .abcd/.work.local/; never commit scratch output into tracked directories.

Keep what is used again out of the host's scratchpad: anything a later turn, session or agent reruns or reads — a helper script, a queue ticket, a log, pull-request text, a handover — goes in the main checkout's .abcd/.work.local/scratch/ (logs/ for run output) or a directory under ~/.abcd.noindex/, never in a linked worktree's .abcd/.work.local/, which git worktree remove deletes with the worktree and without asking; a file for that worktree's own work alone may stay in its own tier. A verifier's copy goes outside every working tree, in a directory of its own under ~/.abcd.noindex/ keyed on the root-commit SHA (the session's scratchpad only for a copy the same turn makes and discards). The host's scratchpad (the temporary folder it hands each session) holds only throwaway files for the turn at hand, because it does not survive a reboot or a new session. LIFEBOAT's runtime-artefacts rule says what stays out of tracked directories; OPINIONS' user's-directory rule says where a tool may create one.

Before writing a helper script, check whether an abcd command already does the job: `abcd --help` lists the commands and each command page says what one does. A preflight, for one, is a plain `make preflight`, which gates itself at `abcd implement load --wait`, and a lone race run outside it is `abcd implement load --wait -- go test -race ./...`, never a hand-written waiter; LOAD's waiter rule says what the gate waits on. Write your own only when no command does it, keep it in the main checkout's .abcd/.work.local/scratch/ as the rule above says, and capture the gap as an issue so abcd can add the command.
Never commit, print, or paste secrets, tokens, or .env contents; reference them by name.
Never put absolute local paths in anything that leaves the machine — use repo-relative paths.
Never name a private repo in commits, PRs, issues, or docs; describe it generically.

Never commit hostnames, IP addresses, MAC addresses, or other live network identifiers; redact or omit them, and use reserved documentation values (RFC 5737, RFC 3849, RFC 2606, RFC 7042) only where an illustrative example is needed.

Prefer SOTA, adversary-filtered: where a choice has a credible state-of-the-art answer that is the presumptive pick, but challenge it for fit against this repo's preferences before adopting; a remedy proposed for an issue, or chosen in an autonomous run, cites its grounds, a primary-source state-of-the-art check where the fix depends on outside practice — see .abcd/development/principles/prefer-sota.md.
One canonical primitive: before adding a generic-smelling primitive, find its canonical home and extend it; never add a third copy — see .abcd/development/principles/one-canonical-primitive.md.
Evaluator outside the loop: the reviewer/challenger is independent of whoever proposed the option — see .abcd/development/principles/evaluator-outside-the-loop.md.
Verifier selects, gates decide: a verdict is a proposal; the human's adoption is the gate — see .abcd/development/principles/verifier-selects-gates-decide.md.
Loud staging: a stage that no-ops or degrades must say so; never manufacture a false green — see .abcd/development/principles/loud-staging.md.
Script-first MVP: earn each tool rung; the smallest documented protocol is the MVP before automation — see .abcd/development/principles/script-first-mvp.md.

Memory graduates to the record: a lesson whose 'why' is a correction any agent should receive belongs in the repo's committed record — the AGENTS.md conventions section, a custom domain in .abcd/rules.json, or a ledger capture — never only in one user's local agent memory, which is for facts about that user and machine; a memory item recalled twice is a graduation candidate — see .abcd/development/principles/memory-graduates-to-record.md.

Pre-existing is not a defence: a defect confirmed while doing other work is fixed, or deferred OUT LOUD as a recorded decision naming the finding and the reason — never filed and stepped over, and never carried past a release about that class of defect. The release cut refuses on a major/critical record captured since the anchor tag and still open; the recorded deferral (`deferred_after` + `deferral_reason` on the record) is the only way past — see .abcd/development/principles/pre-existing-is-not-a-defence.md.

The user's directory is theirs: a tool never creates directories beside the user's projects or anywhere the user did not hand over; a worktree goes under ~/.abcd.noindex/worktrees/ keyed on the root-commit SHA, and a verifier's copy goes outside every working tree, in a directory of its own under ~/.abcd.noindex/ keyed on the root-commit SHA (the session's scratchpad only for a copy the same turn makes and discards); other scratch, an export for instance, may go in the checkout's .abcd/.work.local/ tier — see .abcd/development/principles/the-users-directory-is-theirs.md.
The full set of opinionated conventions lives in .abcd/development/principles/ — read the relevant file rather than guessing the convention.
